description.narrative: Improve the quality of services in administering social insurance and strengthen the regulatory framework for people with disabilities and hazardous occupations.

This project supports pension reform implementation and strenthening of social insurance administration. Areas identified and under consideration include i) development of central registry of socially insured individuals with a second pillar registry module, ii) Central Disability Certification Coordination Unit, iii) revision of the list of hazardous occupations eligible for early retirementwith extended service period, and iv) development of capacity to administer and coordinate professional rehabilitation of persons with disabilities.

title.narrative: Proportion of multiple disability benefit beneficiaries under 26 years undertaking single disability certification through established CDCCU using unified methodology for disability assessment

comment.narrative: Over time, it is expected that because of the methodology unification and institutional coordination, the persons who already have a valid disability certificate will no longer need other certificates to apply for other benefits

title.narrative: Share of beneficiaries satisfied with responsiveness of the grievance redress mechanism

comment.narrative: This indicator monitors the beneficiary satisfaction with the responsiveness of the grievance redress mechanism.

actual.value: No complaints or grievances have been recorded during the reporting period. Therefore, data on beneficiary satisfaction with the responsiveness of the grievance redress mechanism is not yet available.

title.narrative: Communication campaigns developed and implemented (SURS, CDCCU, disability employment)

comment.narrative: This indicator tracks the communication campaigns developed and implemented for the project activities (in the areas of SURS, CDCCU, and disability employment). The three planned campaigns will be part of a single public relations package.

actual.value: To boost the stakeholders engagement, primarily of persons with disabilities and their organizations, the PMU and MSPDY, with Bank assistance, were going to hold the Conference “New Approaches in Disability Assessment and Productive Value in the Economy,” in Skopje. Initially scheduled for March 25, 2025, the event was postponed due to the Kocani tragedy and is now tentatively rescheduled for May or June 2026 (to be decided). The project has integrated citizen engagement across all major reform areas, particularly in disability assessment, disability employment, and early retirement policy. During this period, work was initiated on the development of a Citizen Engagement and Communication Strategy. The strategy, finalized in October 2025, will serve as a guiding framework for both internal and external communication, ensuring coherence, transparency, and greater impact in advocacy and stakeholder engagement. A targeted, and multi-channel communication plan has also been drafted.

title.narrative: Percentage of centrally maintained records of socially insured individuals shared by all social insurance agencies

comment.narrative: Share of social insurance records containing information on employment status, service record, past earnings, and other data relevant for all social insurance agencies. Currently, records are maintained individually by agencies, while in the future they will be maintained centrally by SURS.

title.narrative: Proportion of insured population whose social insurance information is centrally available to all social insurance agencies.

comment.narrative: The percentage of insured population whose data is entered into the new single unified register and is available for reference and processing to relevant agencies.

title.narrative: Average time to transfer second pillar funds to individual accounts

comment.narrative: Time between collection of second pillar contribution and its receipt on the individual account.

title.narrative: Proportion of individual pension service and earnings records in PIOM that are consolidated

comment.narrative: The percentage of individuals with fully registered and accounted-for service years (i.e. with clean and complete data on paid contributions, wages earned, length of work.)

target.value: Actuarial department fully staffed and operational.

comment.narrative: The World Bank team conducted a PROST model training during the Pension Policy Technical Assistance Mission, which was held from February 3 to February 7, 2025. This PROST model training strengthened the capacity of key governmental agencies (PIONM, MAPAS, MSPDY, and the Fiscal Council) to analyze the current pension system's coverage, fiscal sustainability, adequacy, and the impacts of parametric and systemic pension reforms.

actual.value: - The PDIFNM drafted its institutional strategy and systematization, including the establishment of an actuarial department - The new actuarial (or long-term forecast) department is expected to be fully staffed by November 2025, including at least two specialists who have already received training under SIAP. Further staff training is planned to be delivered from December 2025 to February 2026.

title.narrative: Law on Employment of Persons with Disabilities enacted

baseline.value: Current law mainly treats employment through sheltered companies.

comment.narrative: The MSPDY formed a task force of three legal representatives in January 2025, coordinated by a PMU expert. The task force is responsible for fine-tuning the Law by the end of March 2025, with the assistance of an SIAP legal consultant hired by the PMU. This updated version of the Law will be subject to a new round of public consultations, after which it will be sent to the Parliament by the end of April 2025.

actual.value: The draft Law on Employment of Persons with Disabilities (2022 version) underwent a comprehensive revision, resulting in the new "Draft Law on Professional Rehabilitation and Supported Employment for Persons with Disabilities." After multi-stakeholder consultations (in June 2025), the law was put on hold during the electoral period. In November 2025, the law was published in the Single National Electronic Registry Regulations (ENER) before being formally submitted to the Government, for submission to Parliament for final adoption.

title.narrative: List of jobs declared as hazardous and arduous (Extended Service Period /ESP/ list) revised and enacted

target.value: ESP list revised and enacted (through pension legislation)

comment.narrative: This indicator looks at a necessary revision/optimization of the ESP-listed jobs defined as hazardous and arduous by the pension legislation.

actual.value: - The SIAP consultant had finalized revisions to the ESP list, covering all job positions in both private and public sectors, including the Ministry of the Interior, the Ministry of Defense, and related national security agencies. The ESP list was finalized after public consultations (held on February 19, 2025) and institutional reviews of the security-related ministries (in October 2025). However, the adoption of the final ESP list is still pending. - Based on the ESP final list, the consortium responsible for monitoring the SURS implementation has begun preparing the technical specifications for the Registry of hazardous and arduous jobs and employers. A contract for developing this Registry is expected to be signed by March 2026. According to the experts estimation, this Registry will not be finalized by the current SIAP closing date (June 30, 2026), which would also impact the finalization of SURS system development.

title.narrative: Single unified registry of socially insured individuals developed and functional

comment.narrative: SURS means a unified, simplified, and centralized registration and database system to social insurance hosted and organized as an independent entity under MLSP, which includes a standardized, transparent, and centralized process of registration of insured individuals, serves all social insurance agencies and the tax administration, and the insured population; and maintains a single unified central database of socially-insured persons and their contribution history. “Operational” means that it takes over all registries of insured persons of all categories of social insurance into a single and central registration function and is able to deliver that information to other agencies as needed.

actual.value: - Progress toward establishing the Single Unified Registry System (SURS) remains ongoing. - The amended SURS Law is currently undergoing the Governmental procedure, and the SURS bylaws are being revised accordingly - The official appointment of the SURS Director and the establishment of the SURS Agency have been postponed, pending the adoption of the amended SURS Law. - The consortium for SURS software development has submitted the final version of the Inception Report and Business Analysis, with the Business Analysis currently under review - Workshops with all relevant institutions (HIF, NAE, PRO, MAPAS, and PDIFNM) were conducted to clarify business processes and define data migration pathways in preparation for SURS software implementation - The hardware equipment for the primary location has been delivered, and the contract for delivery to the secondary location has been signed - The consortium responsible for monitoring SURS software development has submitted the Inception Report.

title.narrative: Central coordination unit for unified disability assessment (CDCCU) functional

comment.narrative: The regulations for putting in place the central coordination unit are enacted, and unit is in place

actual.value: By the end of October 2025, the company developing the CDCCU software and the National Registry of Persons with Disabilities had already finalized version zero of the CDCCU software for testing. The problem is that the CDCC Unit is not yet operational. Therefore, there is no place to install CDCCU_v0 and personnel to start testing it. Also, data migration is not yet possible. Thus, establishing the Central Disability Certification Coordination Unit (CDCCU) within the MSPDY is crucial for the implementation of this subcomponent 2.1. This is pending approval of the MSPDY's systematization, which was developed and submitted to the Ministry of Public Administration for review and approval. By mid-November 2025, no official feedback or decisions have been received. Although the premises for the new CDCC Unit have been identified, the allocation of office spaces is still pending.

title.narrative: Single registry of persons with disabilities developed and functional

comment.narrative: This indicator requires the creation and putting into operation of a registry of all persons with disability certificates in North Macedonia.

actual.value: The protocols for migration of existing data on persons with disabilities from the information systems of various institutions/commissions (SWIS, Moj Termin, Veterans Affairs, and War Disabled Administration System, PIOM System – Department for Assessment of Working Ability, Department for the Functional Assessment of Children and Youth with Disabilities, etc.) are still to be signed. Still, the conditions and a template have been agreed upon.

title.narrative: Average time to issue a disability certificate

comment.narrative: Average number of days spent from the application for a disability certificate is submitted until the disability certificate is issued or until a formal decision for those who were rejected is submitted to the applicant for the persons who were issued certificates or rejection formal decisions in the previous month. The indicator is calculated for all 5 types of disability certificates.

title.narrative: Enacted unified methodology for disability assessment and determination

comment.narrative: The project promotes developing and introducing a single methodology for disability assessment and determination that will apply to all types of disability-related benefits/services legislated and provided by public sources.

actual.value: The consortium (contracted on February 20, 2025) to conduct the data collection activities of the pilot study submitted and obtained approval for the Inception Report (on June 23, 2025), hired and trained 26 professionals (in July 2025), and developed an online application. The pretesting of the data collection tools was scheduled for mid-September 2025, with the fieldwork planned to start by the end of September 2025. However, in the political context of local elections, the data collection was put on hold. As of mid-November 2025, the fieldwork is pending clearance from the Ministry of Health for the existing assessment commissions to cooperate with the pilot study. Due to this delay, realizing the 2,000 estimates by June 2025 translates into 285 assessments per month, which is a real operational risk – both in terms of the number of persons who will submit requests, and in terms of the capacity of the research teams (3 teams × 5 assessments per day, every working day).

title.narrative: Share of citizen engagement activities, which result in inputs incorporated in the project design.

comment.narrative: The indicator monitors how many events out of all events for the CE engagement (formatted workshops, focus groups) resulted in feedback that is incorporated in project outputs and activities.

title.narrative: Centers for professional rehabilitation of persons with disabilities developed

comment.narrative: The regional rehabilitation centers will be regulated through the Law on Employment of Persons with Disabilities. In addition to rehabilitation, the regional centers will be allowed to possibly include other activities relevant to the social inclusion of persons with disabilities, such as centers for disability assessment or social services (daycare, respite, club, etc.).

actual.value: A study visit to Slovenia was organized in September 2025 to learn from international best practices on professional rehabilitation and disability-inclusive employment systems. A second visit took place in early October 2025, in Croatia. However, the activities related to the rehabilitation (REHA) centers for persons with disabilities depend on the adoption of the new "Draft Law on Professional Rehabilitation and Supported Employment for Persons with Disabilities." Suppose the law adoption is prolonged by 6-9 months, as the MSPDY Deputy Minister estimated. In that case, the REHA centers' related activities are unlikely to fit within the remaining project time and would realistically start in July 2026 and be completed by June 2028.
